model.description: Randomized directed APSP with polynomially bounded integer weights and no negative cycles. Monte Carlo: the algorithm may read uniformly random words, one step each; it must halt within the time bound on every random outcome and be correct with probability at least 2/3 on every input (the claims here have error at most \(n^{-C}\) for every constant \(C\)). Same word RAM, weight and word-length quantifiers, input and output as the deterministic APSP board: edge-presence and weight matrices in, reachability flags and distances for every ordered pair out.

score.definition: Worst-case \(O(n^\alpha)\), Monte Carlo, error probability at most \(1/3\) on every input.

records.title: Ruhollah Majdoddin Monte Carlo APSP in time O(n^2.98989) (version 2)

dependencies.statement: The running-time bound rests on the written proof; the companion Lean projects do not formalise running times. No site rerun.

The paper does not define a randomized machine. It draws uniform random masks and a uniformly random prime and counts steps of a word RAM with O(log N)-bit words. Reading each random word as one step is our interpretation of the Monte Carlo model.

majdoddin-apsp-randomized-2026.proof_status: The author states a Monte Carlo algorithm for directed APSP with polynomially bounded integer weights and no negative cycles: error probability at most n^(-C) for every constant C, worst-case time O(n^2.98989). The paper proves the exponent 2.9898857... and rounds up in the fifth decimal. It is a written proof, not peer reviewed; the running time is not formalised in Lean and no Lean file checks it. The paper does not define a randomized machine: it draws uniform random masks and a uniformly random prime, and counts steps of a word RAM with O(log N)-bit words. This board reads each random word as one step. No independent rerun.
majdoddin-apsp-randomized-2026.comparison_status: Corollary 23.5: APSP on directed n-vertex graphs with integer weights of absolute value n^O(1) and no negative cycles has a Monte Carlo algorithm with error probability n^(-C), for every constant C, in worst-case time O(n^2.98989). The proof computes the exponent 2.9898857... and absorbs the polylogarithmic factors by rounding up in the fifth decimal, so O(n^2.98989) is the stated bound. The problem is the one of the deterministic board (directed, polynomially bounded integer weights, no negative cycles, all ordered pairs). The paper does not define a randomized word RAM: it draws uniform random masks and a uniformly random prime and counts steps of a word RAM with O(log N)-bit words. Reading each random word as one step is our interpretation, as in the Monte Carlo statement proposed in issue 26. Source comparison, not a proof check.
majdoddin-apsp-randomized-2026.scope: Directed integer weights of polynomial magnitude, no negative cycles, all-pairs distances; Monte Carlo, worst-case time.
majdoddin-apsp-randomized-2026.exact_statement: APSP on directed n-vertex graphs with integer weights of absolute value n^O(1) and no negative cycles has a Monte Carlo algorithm with error probability n^(-C), for every constant C, in worst-case time O(n^2.98989).
majdoddin-apsp-randomized-2026.score_interpretation: Attained bound O(n^2.98989) for a Monte Carlo algorithm with error at most n^(-C); the proof computes 2.9898857... and rounds up.
majdoddin-apsp-randomized-2026.date_precision: GitHub commit timestamp in UTC; observation time separate.

majdoddin-apsp-randomized-2026.credits: Ruhollah Majdoddin. Builds on Alman and Vassilevska Williams (arXiv:2610.06783), the residue folding of the working note of shreshth-s, Schonhage's five-term partial-product tensor and the author's version 1. The paper says it was written with Anthropic's Claude models under the author's direction.
majdoddin-apsp-randomized-2026.credit_note: Ruhollah Majdoddin gives a Monte Carlo algorithm for directed APSP in O(n^2.98989), below every deterministic exponent on the board. The paper says its Monte Carlo reductions need only the parities of the counts that the deterministic reductions compute.
